framework.name: Choose, Tell, Check, Own

habits.kid: Is this a job for Bloop, for me, or for both?
habits.teen: Decide whether, when and how to use AI. Can is not should.
Give context: the result, the steps, how the helper should act.
Judge the answer, how it got there, how it behaved. Ask again better.

habits.kid: Keep secrets. Say when AI helped.
habits.teen: Privacy, honesty about AI use, you answer for what you hand in.

evidence_types.think: A reflection or rule in the child's own words

framework.attribution_note: Inspired by ideas in the AI Fluency Framework (Dakan, Feller, Anthropic, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Original wording and activities. Internal only; no endorsement implied.
game_rules: One game for all kids. No girls' or boys' versions.
Kids pick the theme, the mechanic stays the same.
Mix play motives: compete, cooperate, build, tell stories.
Every game maps to one lesson and habit, leaves a made/how/think proof and follows the track's tool rule.

tracks.tool_rule: Grown-up at the keyboard. Mostly unplugged or Bloop simulator.
tracks.goal: Knows AI is a helper people taught, asks clearly, spots silly mistakes, keeps 3 secret rules, says made with Bloop.

catalog_entry.title: Bloop's Helper Habits
catalog_entry.desc: Learn four helper habits with Bloop: choose, tell, check and own. Catch Glitch's mistakes and keep your secrets safe.

lessons.title: Bloop Is a Helper
lessons.idea: AI is a program people taught. It helps, you decide.
lessons.activity: Who did it? cards: toaster, Bloop, kid, mom. Sort what people do and what helpers do.
lessons.at_home: Find 3 helpers at home.

lessons.title: Robot or Me?
lessons.idea: Some jobs are yours because they're fun or come from your heart.
lessons.activity: Picture cards sorted into Me / Bloop helps / Together.
lessons.at_home: Ask which job they'd never give a robot.

lessons.title: Tell Bloop Exactly
lessons.idea: Clear words get the right picture.
lessons.activity: Silly robot game, then who + what + color request to the image tool, grown-up types.
lessons.at_home: Play silly robot at dinner.

lessons.title: Oops, Glitch!
lessons.idea: Helpers make mistakes. We check.
lessons.activity: Find 5 Glitch mistakes in a picture, then count mistakes in a generated picture.
lessons.at_home: Spot one voice-assistant mistake together.

lessons.title: Secrets Stay With Me
lessons.idea: Never tell a computer your name, home, school or password.
lessons.activity: Safe or secret? sorting game.
lessons.at_home: Stick the card next to the tablet.

lessons.title: Made With Bloop
lessons.idea: Say when AI helped.
lessons.activity: Storybook page stamped made by me + Bloop; learn the 4 gestures.

proof.what: Signed page + My Robot Rules card

lessons.at_home: Child explains the 4 gestures.

game_notes.age_needs: Many can't read yet, 10-15 min per activity, learn by moving and pretending, losing hurts, strictest age about girl/boy things. No reading, movement, whole group vs Glitch, neutral themes.
rules: Never princesses or cars as the only option, no pink/blue coding.

games.name: Teach Bloop
games.how: Kids train Bloop (puppet or grown-up) with cat / not cat cards. Only orange cats shown, so Bloop says a black cat is not a cat.
games.why: Makes AI is a program people taught physical. Bad examples make a bad AI, without the words data or bias.

games.name: Silly Robot
games.how: A kid gives orders, the grown-up robot takes them literally.
games.why: Kids love bossing an adult and watching them fail. They feel why clear words matter.

games.name: Spot the Glitch
games.how: AI pictures with 5 hidden mistakes. The group finds all 5 before the timer and Glitch loses.
games.why: Spot-the-difference is a skill they already have, no reading. Group vs Glitch, so no kid loses.

games.name: Safe or Secret? Run
games.how: Grown-up names an item. Kids run to the green (safe) or red (secret) corner.
games.why: Movement and repetition make the 3 secret rules stick. A two-way choice fits this age.

games.name: Story Dice
games.how: Roll 3 picture dice: who + what + where. The kid says the sentence, the grown-up types it into the image tool.
games.why: Turns the who + what + color request into play. Ends with a page parents see.

tracks.tool_rule: No personal chatbot accounts. Bloop chat simulator or parent runs the tool.
tracks.goal: Decides which tasks go to AI, writes a 3-part request, tests AI on known answers, asks for hints not answers, keeps data private, signs AI use.

catalog_entry.title: You're the Boss of AI
catalog_entry.desc: Decide what AI should do, ask it clearly, test it on things you know and use it as a coach, not an answer machine.

lessons.title: Who's the Boss?
lessons.idea: AI is a tool. You set the goal.
lessons.activity: Pairs role-play a literal AI, then swap. Meet the Boss Checklist.
lessons.at_home: Child explains the 4 habits.

lessons.title: Three Piles
lessons.idea: AI does it / AI helps, I decide / only me. Can is not should.
lessons.activity: Sort 12 real homework and hobby tasks.
lessons.at_home: Sort this week's homework together.

lessons.title: The 3-Question Recipe
lessons.idea: What I want + how + what kind of helper.
lessons.activity: Vague vs recipe request in the Bloop chat simulator.
lessons.at_home: Write one recipe request for a family task.

lessons.title: Ask Again, Better
lessons.idea: The first answer is a draft.
lessons.activity: 3 rounds to a great hobby quiz, noting each change.
lessons.at_home: Child shows what changed from round 1 to 3.

lessons.title: Test the Robot
lessons.idea: Test AI on what you know before you trust it.
lessons.activity: 5 expert questions, score the answers, Glitch scoreboard.
lessons.at_home: Ask what AI got wrong about your town.

lessons.title: Hint, Not Answer
lessons.idea: A coach makes you smarter. An answer machine makes you slower.
lessons.activity: Same problem with answer vs hint request; compare.
lessons.at_home: Use the coach card on real homework, parent watching.

lessons.title: Data Detective
lessons.idea: Share only what the task needs.
lessons.activity: Mark personal info on a fake form, rewrite the request without it.
lessons.at_home: Check what family apps know about you.

lessons.title: Boss Project + Family AI Deal
lessons.idea: Use all 4 habits on one project.
lessons.activity: Mini project, AI note, family AI deal signed with a parent.
lessons.at_home: Put the deal on the fridge.

game_notes.age_needs: Read well, love rules, fairness, points, codes and mysteries, ready for some competition, want to be the expert.
themes: chosen by the kid: own expert topic
rules: Swap the keyboard every round so both kids in a pair type.

games.name: Barrier Drawing
games.how: Back to back. The Boss describes a picture, the Bot draws only what was said. Swap.
games.why: Classic communication game. The failure is visible and funny, role swap is built in.

games.name: Three Piles Court
games.how: Sort 12 task cards into 3 piles. Another pair can object, and you defend the card in one sentence.
games.why: Can vs should needs arguing. This age is obsessed with fairness, so debate keeps them hooked.

games.name: Prompt Chef
games.how: Pairs get a target result. Fewest rounds in the simulator to hit it wins.
games.why: Makes ask again, better a score. The round log is the how proof.

games.name: Stump the Robot
games.how: Each kid picks a topic they're the expert on. Ask Bloop 5 questions, score it.
games.why: The kid is the expert, the AI is the student. Own topic fits every interest with no gender label.

games.name: Two Truths and a Bot
games.how: Bloop gives 3 facts, 1 is made up. Pairs vote on the fake, then check.
games.why: 5-minute warm-up for any lesson. Trains don't trust, check.

games.name: Hint Ladder
games.how: Solve a puzzle. Each hint costs 1 step, asking for the answer sends you back to the start.
games.why: Rewards the coach habit with points instead of a lecture about cheating.

games.name: Data Detective Escape
games.how: A fake class profile hides personal info. Each correct cross-out gives one digit of the lock code.
games.why: Mystery and escape themes peak at this age. Clear win.

tracks.tool_rule: Age 12: parent account, parent in the room. 13-14: teen account with parental consent. Never Claude (18+).
tracks.goal: Explains why chatbots make things up, plans AI use across a project, builds context notes, verifies in two sources, compares tools, writes a personal AI policy, presents with an AI use statement.

catalog_entry.title: AI Pilot
catalog_entry.desc: Be the pilot, not the passenger: plan when to use AI, give it context, check every claim and write your own AI rules.

lessons.title: Pilot or Passenger
lessons.idea: 3 ways AI works: Do-for-me, Think-with-me, Run-for-me.
lessons.activity: Classify 10 real AI uses.
lessons.at_home: Find one Run-for-me AI at home.

lessons.title: Why AI Makes Things Up
lessons.idea: Chatbots predict likely words. Likely isn't true.
lessons.activity: Next-word game, then ask AI about a made-up historical person.
lessons.at_home: Explain likely isn't true in one minute.

lessons.title: Should AI Do This?
lessons.idea: Ask what the task is for: learning, speed or people.
lessons.activity: Break a poster project into 8 steps, tag and defend.
lessons.at_home: Map one real school project.

lessons.title: Context Is King
lessons.idea: AI knows only what you give it.
lessons.activity: Reusable About my project note; same request with and without it.
lessons.at_home: Parent checks the note has no personal data.

lessons.title: Set Up a Study Buddy
lessons.idea: Describe the result, the steps and the behavior.
lessons.activity: Build a hint-giving quiz buddy, try to break it, fix the setup.
lessons.at_home: Use the buddy on one real topic.

lessons.title: The Checking Loop
lessons.idea: Name one exact problem per round.
lessons.activity: 3 rounds on an explainer paragraph with precise fixes.
lessons.at_home: Ask about the worst first-draft mistake.

lessons.title: Two Sources + Tool Face-off
lessons.idea: Verify in 2 independent sources. Tools differ.
lessons.activity: Fact-check 3 claims; compare two chatbots.
lessons.at_home: Fact-check one viral post together.

lessons.title: Your Data, Your Call
lessons.idea: Typed data can be stored and used for training. Age limits exist for a reason.
lessons.activity: Read real privacy settings with a parent; redact a sample text.
lessons.at_home: Turn off training on data in family AI tools.

lessons.title: My AI Rules
lessons.idea: When I use AI, my red lines, how I tell teachers, how I keep skills sharp.
lessons.activity: Draft, peer review, parent signs.
lessons.at_home: Parent signs and adds one family rule.

lessons.title: Demo Day
lessons.idea: Show the process, not just the result.
lessons.activity: Team project with process log and How we used AI statement.
lessons.at_home: Parents attend the demo.

game_notes.age_needs: Friends and status matter most, hate anything babyish, want real tools and real stakes, love beating the system. Purpose, story and team roles keep girls in tech; competition and beat the system keep many boys in. Use both.
rules: Rotate team roles (lead, typer, checker, presenter) every lesson.

games.name: Next Word
games.how: Teams guess the next word. You score when you match the most common guess.
games.why: They act like a language model and feel likely isn't true. Explains the mechanism with no math.

games.name: Fake Historian
games.how: Invent a person, ask AI about them, teams race to list every invented fact.
games.why: The shock moment: AI lies confidently. Memorable and filmable (launch reel, day 9).

games.name: Should AI? Court
games.how: Mock trial: Sam used AI for the essay. Prosecutor, defense, judge, jury, clerk.
games.why: Teens love arguing about fairness. Judge and clerk roles let quiet kids take part too.

games.name: Red Team the Study Buddy
games.how: Team A sets up a buddy that only gives hints. Team B tries to make it give answers. Fix, then swap.
games.why: Beat the system is the strongest motivator at this age. They learn instruction writing by attacking and defending it. Only goal allowed: get the homework answer.

games.name: Blind Chatbot Taste Test
games.how: Same question to two chatbots, answers shown as A and B. Teams judge blind, then reveal.
games.why: Breaks brand loyalty: judge quality, not the name.

games.name: Fact or Fake: Feed Edition
games.how: Real viral posts from their platforms. Teams check each in 2 independent sources against the clock.
games.why: Their own feed means real stakes and a skill they use daily.

games.name: Make a Game
games.how: Demo Day project: quiz game, text adventure or game design doc made with AI help, plus a How we used AI log.
games.why: At this age making a game beats playing one. Teams pick the theme, so everyone has a way in.

parent_trust_statement: We use AI to help draft lesson ideas and pictures. A human teacher writes the final lessons, checks every fact, and decides what kids see. Kids never chat with AI alone.
